principles: Reuse the existing resolveStorySignedWorkspace() — no new resolver
cwd-only: never change git command text, gate semantics, or bootstrap
Null/unresolved gitRoot falls back to projectRoot so plain repos are byte-identical
Reroute via the existing dependency-injection seams (default readers / git call sites), keeping signatures back-compatible
Prove correctness with a wrapper-root vs plain-repo test pair (a wrong-tree pass is worse than a block)
drivers: Wrapper-root projects (metadataRoot not a git repo) are blocked from story_discard / validate --channel / validate --concept
A cwd regression could make a gate FALSELY PASS by running git against the wrong tree — must be test-guarded
The resolver already knows the right root; the consumers just don't ask it

options.name: A: resolve authoritativeCwd at handler entry, thread into readers + worktree git sites, null-fallback to projectRoot
pros: Single source of truth (the existing resolver)
cons: Must touch ~14 sites across 4 files; needs careful threading through DI seams

options.name: B: per-call git -C <root>
cons: Scatters root logic, risks drift from the single resolver — rejected

chosen: A: resolve authoritativeCwd at handler entry, thread into readers + worktree git sites, null-fallback to projectRoot
rationale: The resolver already computes the configured gitRoot; rerouting the consumers through it is mechanical and keeps one source of truth. The null-fallback preserves byte-identical behavior for non-wrapper-root repos, and a wrapper-root vs plain-repo test pair guards against both the original block and a wrong-tree false pass.

preMortem.scenario: A rerouted git op runs against the wrong tree and a gate FALSELY PASSES
preMortem.trigger: cwd resolved to an unintended path or fallback applied when a real gitRoot exists
preMortem.consequence: validate --channel/--concept passes against the wrong repo, hiding real problems
preMortem.mitigation: Wrapper-root test asserts each rerouted site runs in the resolved gitRoot; plain-repo test asserts projectRoot; assert exact cwd, not just success

preMortem.scenario: Plain (non-wrapper) repos break because the fallback didn't trigger
preMortem.trigger: resolver returns null/unresolved but code doesn't fall back to projectRoot
preMortem.mitigation: Explicit null/unresolved -> projectRoot fallback; plain-repo test asserts byte-identical behavior and cwd==projectRoot

preMortem.scenario: A git site is missed (not all ~14 rerouted)
preMortem.consequence: Wrapper-root projects still partially fail (e.g. discard fixed but validate not)
preMortem.mitigation: Grep all four files for cwd:/projectRoot/root + execFileSync/git() call sites; reroute each; tests cover channel + concept + cluster-sync + discard + merge

preMortem.scenario: Threading authoritativeCwd changes a reader/helper signature and breaks other callers
preMortem.consequence: Compile errors or behavior change for unrelated callers
preMortem.mitigation: Thread via existing default-reader injection / optional cwd param defaulting to projectRoot; build + full validate before advancing

preMortem.scenario: A call site lacks the story context needed to call the resolver
preMortem.mitigation: Resolve at the handler entry where story context exists and pass cwd down; where unavailable, fall back to projectRoot (documented)
